title: Phumulani Evidence-Based Outcomes & Anonymized Impact Case Studies
summary: Anonymized longitudinal outcomes and case study summaries demonstrating long-term housing stability and economic self-sufficiency.
content: Phumulani tracks long-term outcomes at 6, 12, and 24 months post-program completion, maintaining strict compliance with VAWA Section 1367 by scrubbing all identifying survivor details: (1) Long-term Housing Stability: 91% of survivors exiting the Healing Homes transitional program maintain independent, permanent housing at the 12-month mark. (2) Safety Retention: 96% of participants report no return to an abusive household after engaging in Healing Sisterhood Circles. (3) Economic Advancement: Graduates of the Economic Self-Reliance Lab achieve an average earned income gain of $18,400 per year within 18 months. Case Study A (Anonymized, Cohort 2025): A mother of three who arrived in crisis completed emergency transitional lodging, secured CNA certification through the Workforce Pathway, and now maintains independent housing while mentoring newly arrived circle participants.
keyFacts: 91% 12-month permanent housing stability rate for Healing Homes graduates.
96% long-term safety retention rate for Healing Sisterhood participants.
Average annual earned income increase of $18,400 for Economic Self-Reliance graduates.
100% de-identification of survivor identities and geographic addresses.
Peer-mentorship retention: 42% of graduated survivors return as volunteer peer mentors.
